newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ringgit recovers on commercial dollar selling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers on commercial dollar selling.

text.p: * Ringgit recovers on commercial dollar selling by Malaysian banks, unwinding of long dollar/ringgit overseas
* Higher swaps attract investments to ringgit
* Seen testing 2.4900 a dollar before heading to 2.4750
The ringgit gained in early morning Asian trading on dollar selling by Malaysian corporate sector from 2.4990 a dollar, dealers said on Thursday.
"There is heavy (dollar) selling pressure this morning. Dollar/ringgit could test 2.4900," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said apart from demand from Malaysian corporates, there was also some early unwinding of long dollar/ringgit positions by overseas funds.
"Swaps are also a bit high this morning. On the back of there is some unwinding (of long dollars)," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
But, some fresh dollar buying by Singapore-based banks around 0200 GMT halted the ringgit's rise.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.472/77 a dollar.
